source.title: UU-Mamba: Uncertainty-aware U-Mamba for Cardiac Image Segmentation
source.authors: Ting-Yu Tsai; Li Lin; Shu Hu; Ming-Ching Chang; Hong-Tu Zhu; Xin Wang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training configurations and reports held-out segmentation metrics, but it does not test any listed claim version directly.
record.gate_note: The ablation reports test-set DSC and MSE for U-Mamba trained with CE loss, uncertainty-aware loss, and uncertainty-aware loss plus SAM. It does not report training error, arbitrary-label fitting, or the train-test gap, and does not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness in V7.
record.test_reason: The study applies SAM based on the premise that flatter minima improve generalization and reports segmentation performance. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, train–test gaps, or any other listed version's comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they conclude that uncertainty-aware loss and SAM improve segmentation accuracy and robustness, attributing gains to balancing loss components and seeking flat minima. Flatness, reduced overfitting, and robustness to perturbations are interpretations rather than directly measured outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a medical segmentation model with uncertainty-aware losses and SAM and evaluates segmentation metrics; it does not use the original random-label/generalization setup or any listed version's intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scores vary across the CE-only, uncertainty-aware-loss, and uncertainty-aware-loss-plus-SAM configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Table I reports average DSC of 92.263%, 92.602%, and 92.787%, and average MSE of 0.3843%, 0.3640%, and 0.3304%, for CE loss, uncertainty-aware loss, and uncertainty-aware loss plus SAM, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this ACDC U-Mamba segmentation experiment, uncertainty-aware loss improves reported segmentation metrics, and adding SAM improves them further.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval
record.problems: No training-set metric or train-test gap is reported, so the held-out score changes cannot establish a change in generalization gap. The reported comparisons provide no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with train–test gaps at comparable training loss, and ranking against other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty estimates or training-set metrics are reported. Lower segmentation MSE alone does not establish robustness or a smaller generalization gap. The text does not specify the evaluation split.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum under the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch size under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
